title: Console MVP: Slimdeck curation, scope prunes and rollback checklist
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Context: As part of the Console observability MVP we must reduce client-facing surface area to meet the launch date while preserving the highest-value operator workflows. This ticket documents an explicit scope pruning (‘slimdeck’) across dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown features, the reasons for each cut, trade-offs, and an actionable rollback checklist if removal causes customer regressions.

Scope changes agreed: 
- Dashboard: ship only three aggregate cards (Route Throughput, Error Rate, Avg P99 Latency) for GA. Postpone: per-route token heatmap, interactive drilldown, and golden metric comparisons. Drilldowns will be implemented later as an opt-in beta.
- Tracing: include trace sampling, histogram rollup, and basic event timeline. Postpone: full flamegraph UI, span-level replays, and distributed trace joins across regions.
- Cost breakdown: surface model-level daily cost and token counts; postpone per-request cost attribution, per-user cost filters, and fine-grain token provenance.

Rationale: 
- Schedule pressure: backend infra for per-request attribution has unfinished data-retention and index optimization work that risks launch.
- Cost: per-request attribution multiplies storage and query costs by ~6x on current load profile; deferring reduces monthly telemetry spend.
- Impact: the agreed cuts preserve core incident response and capacity planning needs (latency/err/throughput), which are the highest priority for early adopters.

Trade-offs and mitigation: 
- Visibility gap for some platform customers: we will expose a CSV export endpoint (read-only) with sampled per-request slices for investigations.
- Product telemetry: add two lightweight queries to Console backend to answer top-10 route cost queries in real-time for support (not UI).

Acceptance gating: this ticket defines the acceptance criteria and rollback triggers below.

Links and artifacts: 
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Observability+MVP+PRD
- Slimdeck mockups (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-slimdeck-mockups
- Backend sampling design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/tracing/sampling-design
- Cost delta analysis (spreadsheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1cost-analysis-march
- Spike PR (infra optimizations): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4210

Open questions: 
- Do enterprise customers with Reserved/Dedicated plans get an opt-in for per-request attribution at launch? (Action: sales/AE sync)
- Should CSV exports be available for Private deployments by default, or gated behind enterprise license?
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: GA view loads primary slate (3 cards) in < 400ms on production-1 region when queried for last 1h
Tracing: sampled traces (1%) display event timeline and histogram within 1.2s for 95% of requests in staging telemetry dataset
Cost breakdown: model-level daily cost summary query completes in < 800ms and matches sampling spreadsheet within 3% variance
Telemetry budget: projected telemetry spend for Console observability must be <= 1.5x current infra baseline after cuts
Export path: sampled per-request CSV export endpoint responds within 5s for queries up to 1M rows (async job OK)
Rollout flag: all pruned features behind feature flags for 30-day GA ramp with automated health checks and kill-switch
UX review: Design sign-off on slimdeck mocks and degraded-state messaging (Designer: Lena Ortiz)
decisions: Remove per-route token heatmap from GA and mark as Beta (decision: 2026-03-06, ratified by PM/Eng/Design)
Defer span-level replay and distributed trace joins until index-optimization delivery (decision: 2026-03-07)
Replace per-request cost attribution with sampled daily exports and an aggregated model-level UI (decision: 2026-03-08)
